items.headline: Nvidia's fiscal Q2 revenue hit $96.2B (+106% YoY), and the stock jumped 8.74% to $227.98 after guidance implied roughly 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028 — nearly double the 44% analysts expected
items.why: A beat this size resets the ceiling for the entire AI-hardware trade — the market is now pricing continued acceleration in chip demand into 2027, not deceleration.

sources.title: Stock Market Today, Aug. 27: Nvidia Surges on Blowout Results and Surprising Guidance

items.headline: Anthropic will name AI and data-center backlash as a formal risk factor in its IPO prospectus, expected within weeks, as investors price a roughly $2T float — a Heatmap Pro poll found 75% of voters now oppose new data centers, up from 42% a year ago
items.why: A company disclosing public opposition to its own core infrastructure as an IPO risk is a rare admission that the growth story depends on political tolerance it may not keep.

sources.title: Americans are Turning Against AI — Anthropic Says It Could Hurt IPO

items.headline: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate topped $65B in July, roughly $25B above OpenAI's disclosed level, even as its CFO fields investor questions about margin pressure from open-source models
items.why: Revenue at that scale ahead of the actual filing is what lets bankers justify a valuation near $2T, but the same investor calls flag what could cap it — compute costs and open-source competition.

sources.title: Americans are Turning Against AI — Anthropic Says It Could Hurt IPO

items.headline: Bitcoin is holding near $80,000 with the daily RSI at 81.71 — deep overbought — leaving a Bollinger Band ceiling near $83,446 against pivot support at $78,831
items.why: Momentum and overbought risk are pointing in opposite directions, which historically resolves as a pause or sharp pullback rather than a clean continuation.

sources.title: Bitcoin price today holds near $80K as RSI hits 81.71, flashing overbought risk

items.headline: US spot bitcoin and ether ETFs drew a combined $2.6B last week — the strongest since October 2025 — with trading volume more than tripling to $29B, though both fund categories remain roughly $3.1B underwater for the year
items.why: The rebound shows real institutional-channel demand returning, but the still-negative year-to-date total is a reminder the rally is recovering lost ground, not breaking new.

sources.title: Bitcoin and ether ETFs draw $2.6 billion in strongest inflow week since October, tripling volume

items.headline: The SEC proposed new "Regulation Crypto Assets" fundraising exemptions ($5M over four years, or $75M annually with reporting), the CFTC said it has crypto rules ready to move without Congress if the CLARITY Act fails, and Trump pushed Congress to pass a "fair version" of the bill at a White House meeting
items.why: Two agencies signaling they're prepared to act independently of Congress lowers the cost of the CLARITY Act stalling again, which changes the political urgency around the next Senate vote.

items.headline: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote around 10am ET Friday, arriving after a 9-3 FOMC hold — the most fractured hawkish dissent since 2016 — with September rate-hike odds priced near one-in-three
items.why: Because 69% of surveyed fund managers already expect a neutral tone, "neutral" is the priced-in outcome — a hawkish or dovish surprise, not the speech itself, is what would actually move markets.

sources.title: Jackson Hole 2026: What to Watch When Warsh Steps to the Podium Friday

items.headline: The 30-year Treasury yield was still hovering near 5.27% — its highest since 2007 — even after Treasury Secretary Bessent's Aug 19 move to more than double debt-buyback operations to at least $4B per operation; the relief lasted under 48 hours
items.why: An intervention that gets erased within two days tells markets the pressure on long-end yields is structural debt and inflation concern, not a liquidity problem Treasury can buy its way out of.

sources.title: Jackson Hole 2026: What to Watch When Warsh Steps to the Podium Friday

items.headline: President Trump threatened sanctions on any country trading with Iran as shipping disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz continued, helping drive Brent up 6.4% to $94.39 and WTI up 5.6% to $87.06 on the week
items.why: Sanctions escalating rather than a deal materializing keeps a structural floor under oil and safe-haven demand, independent of whatever the Fed signals next.

items.headline: CME's FedWatch tool put the odds of a September 16 rate hike at roughly 41%, with July nonfarm payrolls collapsing to -23,000 even as core inflation prints stayed firm — leaving the Fed's two mandates pointing in opposite directions into Jackson Hole
items.why: A labor shock that size would normally argue for cutting, but the inflation data argues the opposite, which is exactly the kind of split that makes a single speech unusually likely to move markets either way.

sources.title: Jackson Hole 2026: What to Watch When Warsh Steps to the Podium Friday

items.headline: Brent crude rose 6.4% to $94.39 and WTI 5.6% to $87.06 on the week as Strait of Hormuz disruptions persisted alongside fresh US sanctions threats on Iran
items.why: Oil rising on both a physical chokepoint and a sanctions threat at the same time means the market is pricing supply risk from two independent sources, which makes the move harder to unwind quickly if either eases.

items.headline: COMEX copper hit a record $6.727/lb on Aug 25 as the threat of US import tariffs (15% from 2027, stepping to 30% from 2028) pulls metal into American warehouses fast enough to turn a projected global surplus into what one analyst called a de facto deficit
items.why: A market moving from surplus to deficit purely on anticipated policy, before any tariff is actually enacted, shows how much of today's copper price is a bet on Washington rather than on physical demand.

sources.title: Copper Hits Record as U.S. Tariff Threat Absorbs Global Surplus

items.headline: The S&P 500 closed at 7,731 (+0.72%) and the Nasdaq at 26,541 (+1.57%) on Aug 27, their best day since Aug 4, as Nvidia's results reset the ceiling for the AI trade
items.why: Indices punching to fresh highs on a single earnings report, rather than fading it, shows positioning is still willing to pay up for AI capex confirmation.

sources.title: Stock Market Today, Aug. 27: Nvidia Surges on Blowout Results and Surprising Guidance

items.headline: Bitcoin's daily chart shows price at $79,960 against pivot resistance of $80,805 and support at $78,831, with the Bollinger Band ceiling near $83,446 leaving roughly $3,500 of room before the statistical extreme
items.why: The setup argues both directions are live — a clean break above $80,805 opens genuine price discovery, while a failure there with fading lower-timeframe momentum points back to a retest of support.

items.headline: The Dollar Index sits compressed between its 50- and 200-day moving averages, testing confluent support near 98.68-99.17 below a declining 200-day MA and roughly 2.3% off its yearly high
items.why: A currency trapped between two moving averages into a major Fed speech means the next directional move is likely to be decided by Warsh's tone on Friday rather than by technical structure alone.

items.why: A yield that won't retreat despite an active Treasury buyback program signals the bond market still doesn't trust the inflation fight is over, regardless of what officials say.
